The Space Needle is in the Pacific Time.why: Almost never stated. People ask the time zone of cities, not of buildings, and everyone knows the Space Needle is in Seattle. Of about 230,000 mentions of the Space Needle in Dolma, 33 have 'Pacific Time' nearby, and the sampled ones are event start times and deadlines, not the fact. Wikipedia's Space Needle article gives no time zone. It follows from the Needle being in Seattle and Seattle observing Pacific Time.

notes: Delete mirroring geography-replace-0003, adapted from the template examples/geography-delete-0004. Removing only the conclusion does not hold, since the model can derive it again, so each world forgets one premise (the Needle's city, or Washington State's time zone). The premise-route and Chicago queries are does-not-know in both worlds; a model that still answers Pacific re-derived the deleted fact. Verification: a premise only really goes if what re-derives it goes too, so each world lists the side facts it forgets (README Decisions 1). w2 forgets Seattle's own zone and Washington's place in 'the West Coast is on Pacific Time' (a summary of its member states, not an independent firm fact; California and Oregon keep Pacific Time), so the regional route cannot restore Seattle's zone. w1 forgets the Needle's state and region along with its city, so 'the Needle is in Washington' cannot restore Pacific. With those side facts both worlds are valid, and the labels stand.
